useWhen: The user asks whether a selected document is ready, what is wrong with it, or for a review before sending it.
The user wants structure, consistency and completeness problems in one identified document reported with locations.
nearMiss: A narrow spelling or typo proofread.
Comparing two documents against each other.

inputs.name: document
inputs.description: The document under review: a path to a readable document, or text the user pasted as the review target.

inputs.name: audience
inputs.description: The intended reader of the document, which changes what counts as a missing definition or a misleading claim.

inputs.name: purpose
inputs.description: What the document is meant to achieve, used to judge completeness.

inputs.name: style-guide
inputs.description: A house style guide or template the document should follow.

inputs.name: output-location
inputs.description: Where the new report file is written. Without it, the report is returned in the conversation.

read: The selected document only, plus reference files the user names explicitly.
write: One new report file at a user-chosen location.
The conversation itself, when the user does not want a file.

outputs.name: document quality report
outputs.description: A Markdown report with severity definitions, findings grouped by structure, consistency and completeness, each carrying an exact location, a short quoted fragment and a reason, plus a readiness statement and a closing not-checked list.

successEvidence: Every finding cites a location that can be found in the reviewed document and quotes only a short fragment.
Severity levels are defined in the report and applied consistently across findings.
Findings are grouped by dimension rather than presented as one unordered list.
The report states which dimensions were not checked and why, including visual layout and macro or formula behaviour.
The report states that the reviewed document was not modified.

failureBehaviour.behaviour: Ask which document to review and produce no report for a guessed document.
Report the exact path and why it cannot be reviewed, then stop. Do not substitute another file.
Say which text-extraction capability is missing and for which format. Report no findings rather than guessing from the file name; with partial text, mark the report partial and list the unread parts.
Report the last completed dimension, mark the report partial and list what was not reviewed.
Produce a new report with a distinct name and state what changed since the previous review. Never overwrite the earlier report and never modify the document.
